newsitem.title: UK: Britons brave Arctic weather for New Year revels.
newsitem.headline: Britons brave Arctic weather for New Year revels.

text.p: Britons braved Arctic weather to celebrate the New Year in giant street parties from London to Edinburgh.
As temperatures plunged, Edinburgh threw the biggest party on Tuesday night with 350,000 people celebrating what is known in Scotland as Hogmanay.
Hospitals had to treat more than 300 people. "Most were suffering from acute alcohol abuse to the point of unconsciousness," an official said.
The crowds were so dense that police and paramedics had to use golf buggies to weave through the throng.
Trafalgar Square was the focus of London celebrations with 90,000 people singing, dancing and kissing each other on the stroke of midnight.
Police, fearing that crowds could be crushed, sealed off the square's fountains and the landmark Nelson's Column. Up to 60 people were arrested, mostly for drunkenness.
